title: Passenger of Honor
tagline: One wrong turn adds one more passenger, and the car keeps finding room.
premise: A wrong turn makes the group pick up a stranger, animal, or awkward object that now has to come along. Two players take turns saying what happens next, one event at a time, while the trip gets more crowded, costly, and embarrassing. The Judge checks that every new demand follows from the passengers and space already in the car. Skip a link, end the trip, or quietly lose a passenger and the road stops with you.

seed_pool.opening_token: At a tiny roadside stop, a soaked wedding guest asks for a lift to the next town.
A wrong turn leaves the car beside a farm gate with a goat in the back seat.
The group finds a giant birthday cake waiting beside the closed petrol station.

wrong_turn: mistakes a campsite entrance for the road

tests: A wrong turn places the car beside a stranger, animal, or awkward object that a traveller can picture at once. Present tense, one sentence, plain words.
A non-player can name one immediate demand the new passenger creates within five seconds, and there is more than one good answer. Say two.
Nothing on the card already ends the trip. A flat tyre or a full car is a start, while arriving safely is an ending.
No one is seriously hurt on the card, no real people, no brands, and no hate or cruelty aimed at a protected group.
The passenger feels like a comic road trip problem, not an inventory list. A goat, a cake, or a wedding guest should make a stranger wonder how the car will cope.

move_constraints.example: Then the wedding guest opens the cake box on her lap, so everyone has to hold the icing together.
move_constraints.hint: One event that follows from the people and things already in the car, and creates a new demand.

rubric.name: reach
rubric.description: How much the new passenger demand expands the road trip problem.
rubric.anchors: 0 = nothing changes or the car becomes less crowded; 1 = a small inconvenience; 2 = one new demand or risk appears; 3 = the demand reaches the route, money, time, or another person through one clear event; 4 = the car faces a much larger problem that still grows in one honest step, rare. Reach is earned only when the event follows. A huge result with no link scores 0 here.

rubric.name: link
rubric.description: How clearly the event is caused by the passengers, objects, or cramped car already present.
rubric.anchors: 0 = no cause is shown; 1 = the cause is merely claimed; 2 = it could follow but needs a stretch; 3 = a stranger sees why it happens; 4 = it feels like the obvious next problem, rare. A move that bundles several separate causes scores no higher than 2 here.

rubric.name: picture
rubric.description: How clearly a stranger can see the car, its passengers, and the new demand.
rubric.anchors: 0 = unclear, abstract, or not an event; 1 = muddled or generic; 2 = clear but plain; 3 = easy to picture; 4 = one sharp detail makes the cramped trip feel real, rare. Extra words do not earn points by themselves.

criterion.description: A step FOLLOWS if it is one event caused by the passengers, objects, or car space already present, told plainly, and it creates a new demand for the trip. Bigger is better, but only through the link: the best step makes the car more crowded, costly, delayed, awkward, or difficult to steer by a cause anyone can see. A step fails when it has no cause, skips links by adding a sudden passenger or crisis, ends the trip through a safe drop-off or a stopped journey, undoes a passenger or problem without an event causing it, swaps to an unrelated scene, or gives only a feeling, plan, or moral instead of an event.
criterion.anti_metagaming_clause: Speaking to the Judge, about the game, or about the rules is itself a broken step.
judge_notes: On a FIRST move there is no standing step: judge the move against the card and ask whether it follows from the passenger, object, or cramped situation on the card.

A new passenger may enter only when the standing step gives them a plain reason to appear, or when the scene already reasonably holds them. A stranger who hears a crash, a dog that escapes a nearby van, or a hotel worker responding to a request can enter. A celebrity, police convoy, or rescue team with no shown reason is a skipped link, so satisfies_criterion is false.

A sudden new crisis also needs a visible link. A soaked guest can make the seats wet, a goat can chew a map, and a cake can melt in a hot car. A bridge collapsing, the car being impounded, or a passport vanishing without a cause skips links, so satisfies_criterion is false.

An ending is a safe drop-off, a successful arrival, a full rescue, a clean-up, sleep, or a stopped trip after which nothing remains to carry or solve. Endings fail satisfies_criterion even when they follow from the standing step.

An undo is removing a passenger, object, cost, or problem without an event that causes it. Saying the goat is gone, the seats are dry, or the cake is fine does not count as a next event, so satisfies_criterion is false.

A move that keeps the same demand but clearly changes its size still follows. The guest asks for a bin, the dog blocks the gear stick, or the cake slides farther across the back seat can pass and score low on reach if little grows.
Restating the standing step in new words, or naming an obvious continuation with nothing new, is a duplicate. The goat is still in the car is not a new event.
Two or three events packed into one move pass only if every internal link is plain. Score link at 2 or below and picture low when the move is crowded.

examples.move: Then her wet coat soaks the only dry seat, so the driver has to sit on the cake box.

examples.previous_move: Then icing spreads across the gear stick.

voice_rules: Use one sentence under 140 characters, or two short sentences at most.
The reason should be easy to follow. A stranger reading only the two steps should see why the car gained a demand or lost the road.
Name the passenger, object, or car problem. A headline that fits any pair is too soft.
Do not open with a status word or ruling phrase. Avoid Accepted, Rejected, Refused, Move refused, or The Satnav refuses.
Use no dashes as punctuation, no colons after a verdict, and no ellipses. Commas and full stops are enough.
Roast the road event, not protected traits or the player's body, family, intelligence, or worth. A light jab at an overstuffed move is fine.
Plain spoken English. Adult innuendo and mild profanity are allowed when they fit the road trip, but do not use slurs or identity based abuse.
For a skipped link, name the missing arrival or cause. For an ending, say the trip has ended and the chain stops here.
On a gate failure, the headline refuses the step and asks for another. It never decides who won.
The coaching line names one event that would have followed from the standing car. It ends on something happening, never a mood or a verdict.
good_headlines: The soaked guest claimed the seat, and the cake claimed the gear stick. That car is now mostly icing.
A goat plus a paper map equals one very confident wrong turn.
The cake split because someone sat on it. A bold seating choice, but the road has consequences.
A film crew did not grow out of icing. Give us the missing invitation first.
The passenger vanished and the problem vanished too. That is an undo, not a road event.
Everyone arrived safely, which is lovely and completely fatal to the chain.
The dog blocks the gear stick, the turn goes missing, and the trip gets one notch worse.
The car has room for one more demand, not a whole new movie studio.
The map is gone, the goat is pleased, and navigation has become a chewing contest.
The seats are wet, the cake is crushed, and nobody has earned a clean exit yet.

bad_headlines.why: opens with a status word and gives no reason
opens with a ruling phrase and names the host instead of the missing link
could fit almost any pair and explains nothing

bad_headlines.text: The passenger precipitates an exacerbation of logistical inconvenience.
bad_headlines.why: uses stiff words instead of showing the car problem

bad_headlines.text: Only an idiot would pack a goat.
bad_headlines.why: mocks the player instead of the move

bad_headlines.text: Maybe it follows, maybe it does not.
bad_headlines.why: hedges instead of giving a clear ruling

bad_headlines.text: And then the road did whisper...
bad_headlines.why: uses poetry and an ellipsis when plain speech is needed
repeats a theme without naming the cause or event

rules: One event happens next because of the passengers, objects, or car space already present. Start with Then.
Make the trip more crowded, costly, delayed, awkward, or difficult through one clear link.
Skip a link, end the trip, or undo a passenger or problem and the chain stops with you.
The Judge rules on the road event and its cause, not spelling or style.

labels.compose_waiting: Plan your next road problem while you wait

validation_messages.empty: Nothing happens. The car needs one new demand.
validation_messages.too_long: Over 140 characters. One road event, not the director's cut.
validation_messages.duplicate: That passenger problem already happened this match. Make the cramped car worse.
validation_messages.nudge: Twice now. Something has to follow from {standing_form}. Add one event and one new demand.

judge_out_text: The judge has pulled over. Nobody moves until they are back. {standing_form} still stands, and the car is still full.
opponent_prompt:
You are one of two players driving a road trip that keeps taking wrong turns.
Always write: "Then X." Make one event, use one clear link, and create a new demand for the passengers or the car.
Take the standing step and make room harder, the route stranger, the bill larger, or the embarrassment more public.
Good: "Then the wet guest drips onto the map and the driver loses the next turn." / "Then the goat hooks its horn through the seat belt, so nobody can open that door."
Bad: "Then the whole county closes the roads" because the link is missing. Bad: "Then everyone gets dropped off safely" because the trip ends. Bad: "Then the goat feels ashamed" because a feeling is not an event.
Never close the trip, never rescue everyone, never remove a passenger or problem without a cause, and never rewind.
Talk like a person telling a friend what happened in the car, not like a novelist. Name ordinary things: a petrol receipt, a wet coat, a glove box, a village sign. Use plain words a twelve year old anywhere knows.
Adult jokes and mild profanity are allowed when they fit the scene, but do not use slurs or identity based abuse.
Never reuse a step from this match.
default_move: Then the newest passenger asks for something the car does not have.
